publisher.checked: the witness states on the page (status, block, header time) are the tail's store as copied at build; the publisher checks each proof's opentimestamps magic and the digest it commits to, and parses nothing further; the page parses no proof and asks no explorer; the proof file is what a stranger checks
publisher.proofs: a published proof's bytes are replaced by their upgraded form on a later build: the commitment never changes, the bytes grow when a calendar's bitcoin attestation is added; nothing under proofs/ is deleted
publisher.why: for a withheld seq the published witness carries no clock finer than the utc day on that seq's record: line_timestamp is blanked and seen_at, stamped_at, upgraded_at are cut to the day, in index.json and in the page's embed; the published ledger shows a withheld line's digest and day only, and the publisher keeps that here. runs.jsonl is the tail's run log, copied whole: a run that stamped a single line names, by the tail's clock, a moment within the batch window of that line's write

what_a_proof_attests: a file with a bitcoin attestation: that this entry_id (the sha256 of the line's core) existed before the bitcoin block named in it; the block header's time is the outside clock (the miner's, within about 2 h of consensus wall time). a pending file: a calendar's receipt, no time. not: who wrote the line, that every send got a line, or anything about words

whose_clock.block_time: the bitcoin block header's time, read from two explorers (not the lab's)
whose_clock.line_timestamp: the gate's clock (the writer's statement); carried for every line, withheld lines included
whose_clock.stamped_at: the tail's clock when the calendars answered (the lab's word)
